claim: The polarity protein Crumbs is essential for apical plasma membrane phospholipid-homeostasis in Drosophila larval salivary glands.
source: Here, we report that the polarity protein Crumbs is essential for apical plasma membrane phospholipid-homeostasis and efficient apical secretion.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this finding, which is supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript showing PI(4,5)P2 accumulation upon Crb knockdown.

claim: Crumbs is essential for efficient apical secretion in Drosophila larval salivary glands.
source: Here, we report that the polarity protein Crumbs is essential for apical plasma membrane phospholipid-homeostasis and efficient apical secretion.
evidence: The abstract states this claim, supported by data showing SerpCBD-GFP retention upon Crb knockdown (Figure 1K-M).

claim: Crumbs maintains Rab6-, Rab11- and Rab30-dependent trafficking by recruiting βHeavy-Spectrin and MyosinV to the apical membrane.
source: Through recruiting βHeavy-Spectrin and MyosinV to the apical membrane, Crumbs maintains the Rab6-, Rab11- and Rab30-dependent trafficking and regulates the lipid phosphatases Pten and Ocrl.
evidence: The abstract states this mechanism, supported by data showing loss of apical Rab6, Rab11, and Rab30 upon Crb knockdown (Figure 4) and reduced apical βH-Spec and MyoV (Figures 2 and 3).

claim: Crumbs regulates the lipid phosphatases Pten and Ocrl.
source: Through recruiting βHeavy-Spectrin and MyosinV to the apical membrane, Crumbs maintains the Rab6-, Rab11- and Rab30-dependent trafficking and regulates the lipid phosphatases Pten and Ocrl.
evidence: The abstract states this claim, supported by data showing changes in Pten2-GFP localization (Figure 5I-K) and Ocrl-RFP localization (Figure 5L-N) upon Crb knockdown.

claim: Crumbs knock-down results in increased apical levels of PI(4,5)P2.
source: Crumbs knock-down results in increased apical levels of PI(4,5)P2 and formation of a novel, Moesin- and PI(4,5)P2-enriched apical membrane sac containing microvilli-like structures.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, supported by data showing increased PLCδ-PH-EGFP fluorescence upon Crb knockdown (Figure 5B,C,H).

claim: Crumbs knock-down results in formation of a novel, Moesin- and PI(4,5)P2-enriched apical membrane sac containing microvilli-like structures.
source: Crumbs knock-down results in increased apical levels of PI(4,5)P2 and formation of a novel, Moesin- and PI(4,5)P2-enriched apical membrane sac containing microvilli-like structures.
evidence: The abstract states this finding, supported by confocal imaging showing phospho-Moe and PI(4,5)P2 accumulation in sacs (Figures 2H, 5C) and TEM showing intracellular vesicles with microvilli (Figure 2L').

claim: Epithelia organize as layers or tubes, which form barriers and separate internal biological compartments from the environment.
source: Epithelia can organize as layers or tubes, which form barriers and thus separate internal biological compartments from the environment.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about epithelial tissue organization.

claim: Many epithelia are specialized for absorption or secretion by performing selective and directional transport of nutrients, enzymes and waste products.
source: Many epithelia are specialized for absorption or secretion by performing selective and directional transport of nutrients, enzymes and waste products, which is essential for metazoan life (Cereijido et al., 2004; Rodriguez-Boulan and Macara, 2014; Lemaitre and Miguel-Aliaga, 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Epithelial cells are highly polarized with plasma membrane proteins and lipids distributed asymmetrically into apical and basolateral domains.
source: To perform these functions, epithelial cells are highly polarized: plasma membrane proteins and lipids are distributed asymmetrically into an apical domain facing the environment or a lumen, and a basolateral domain that contacts the neighboring cell and/or a basal lamina.
evidence: This is established knowledge about epithelial cell polarity.

claim: Polarity in epithelial cells is manifested by uneven distribution of organelles, asymmetric cytoskeleton organization and directed trafficking.
source: In addition, polarity is manifested by uneven distribution of organelles, asymmetric cytoskeleton organization and directed trafficking (Rodriguez-Boulan and Macara, 2014; Knust and Bossinger, 2002; Eaton and Martin-Belmonte, 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Several evolutionarily conserved proteins regulate epithelial cell polarity, including members of the apical Crumbs- and PAR-complexes, and the basolateral Scrib-Dlg-Lgl module.
source: Several evolutionarily conserved proteins regulate epithelial cell polarity. These include members of the apical Crumbs- and PAR-complexes, and the basolateral Scrib-Dlg-Lgl module (reviewed in Flores-Benitez and Knust, 2016; Román-Fernández and Bryant, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to review articles.

claim: The Crumbs protein has a large extracellular domain (>2000 aa) and a small intracellular domain (37 aa).
source: The Crumbs (Crb) protein has a large extracellular domain (>2000 aa), and a small intracellular domain (37 aa) (Tepass et al., 1990; Wodarz et al., 1993), which harbors two protein-protein interaction motifs, a C-terminal PDZ (Postsynaptic density/Discs large/ZO-1)-domain binding motif (PBM) and a juxtamembrane FERM (protein 4.1/ezrin/radixin/moesin)-domain binding motif (FBM).
evidence: This structural information is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The Crumbs intracellular domain harbors a C-terminal PDZ-domain binding motif (PBM) and a juxtamembrane FERM-domain binding motif (FBM).
source: The Crumbs (Crb) protein has a large extracellular domain (>2000 aa), and a small intracellular domain (37 aa) (Tepass et al., 1990; Wodarz et al., 1993), which harbors two protein-protein interaction motifs, a C-terminal PDZ (Postsynaptic density/Discs large/ZO-1)-domain binding motif (PBM) and a juxtamembrane FERM (protein 4.1/ezrin/radixin/moesin)-domain binding motif (FBM).
evidence: This structural information is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The PBM of Crumbs is important for cell polarity and can bind Stardust (Sdt) and Par-6.
source: The PBM is important for cell polarity and can bind Stardust (Sdt) and Par-6 (Li et al., 2014; Roh et al., 2002; Bulgakova et al., 2008; Bachmann et al., 2001; Hong et al., 2001; Kempkens et al., 2006; Ivanova et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to previous literature.

claim: The FBM of Crumbs can directly interact with Yurt (Yrt), Expanded (Ex) and Moesin (Moe).
source: The FBM can directly interact with Yurt (Yrt), Expanded (Ex) and Moesin (Moe) (Klebes and Knust, 2000; Laprise et al., 2006; Ling et al., 2010; Wei et al., 2015), FERM-proteins that act as adaptors between membrane proteins and the actin cytoskeleton (Bennett and Baines, 2001; Lemmon et al., 2002; McClatchey, 2014; Sauvanet et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: FERM-proteins act as adaptors between membrane proteins and the actin cytoskeleton.
source: The FBM can directly interact with Yurt (Yrt), Expanded (Ex) and Moesin (Moe) (Klebes and Knust, 2000; Laprise et al., 2006; Ling et al., 2010; Wei et al., 2015), FERM-proteins that act as adaptors between membrane proteins and the actin cytoskeleton (Bennett and Baines, 2001; Lemmon et al., 2002; McClatchey, 2014; Sauvanet et al., 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The FBM of Crb is important for βHeavy-Spectrin (βH-Spec) recruitment to the apical plasma membrane.
source: The FBM of Crb is also important for βHeavy-Spectrin (βH-Spec) recruitment to the apical plasma membrane, and thereby supports the polarized organization of the membrane-associated cytoskeleton (cytocortex) (Wodarz et al., 1995; Richard et al., 2009; Pellikka et al., 2002; Lee et al., 2010; Lee and Thomas, 2011; Médina et al., 2002b).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Several epithelia of crb or sdt mutant Drosophila embryos show severe polarity defects, disruption of cell-cell adhesion and loss of tissue integrity.
source: Several epithelia of crb or sdt mutant Drosophila embryos show severe polarity defects, disruption of cell-cell adhesion and loss of tissue integrity.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature (Tepass and Knust, 1993; Grawe et al., 1996; Tepass et al., 1990; Das and Knust, 2018; Tepaß and Knust, 1990).

claim: Over-expression of Crb in the embryonic epidermis increases the size of the apical membrane.
source: On the other hand, over-expression of Crb in the embryonic epidermis increases the size of the apical membrane (Tepass and Knust, 1993; Grawe et al., 1996; Tepass et al., 1990; Das and Knust, 2018; Tepaß and Knust, 1990).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Similar phenotypes to Drosophila crb mutants have been reported in mouse embryos mutant for Crb2 or Crb3.
source: Similar phenotypes have been reported in mouse embryos mutant for Crb2 or Crb3 (Charrier et al., 2016; Szymaniak et al., 2015; Whiteman et al., 2014; Xiao et al., 2011; Ramkumar et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Drosophila Crb has been associated with regulation of tissue growth via the Hippo pathway.
source: In addition, Drosophila Crb has been associated with other functions, which are independent of its roles in epithelial integrity, such as regulation of tissue growth via the Hippo pathway, regulation of Notch signaling (Das and Knust, 2018; Nemetschke and Knust, 2016; Perez-Mockus et al., 2017; Herranz et al., 2006), as well as photoreceptor morphogenesis and survival under light stress (reviewed in Pocha and Knust, 2013; Bulgakova and Knust, 2009; Genevet and Tapon, 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Drosophila Crb has been associated with regulation of Notch signaling.
source: In addition, Drosophila Crb has been associated with other functions, which are independent of its roles in epithelial integrity, such as regulation of tissue growth via the Hippo pathway, regulation of Notch signaling (Das and Knust, 2018; Nemetschke and Knust, 2016; Perez-Mockus et al., 2017; Herranz et al., 2006), as well as photoreceptor morphogenesis and survival under light stress (reviewed in Pocha and Knust, 2013; Bulgakova and Knust, 2009; Genevet and Tapon, 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Drosophila Crb has been associated with photoreceptor morphogenesis and survival under light stress.
source: In addition, Drosophila Crb has been associated with other functions, which are independent of its roles in epithelial integrity, such as regulation of tissue growth via the Hippo pathway, regulation of Notch signaling (Das and Knust, 2018; Nemetschke and Knust, 2016; Perez-Mockus et al., 2017; Herranz et al., 2006), as well as photoreceptor morphogenesis and survival under light stress (reviewed in Pocha and Knust, 2013; Bulgakova and Knust, 2009; Genevet and Tapon, 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to review articles.

claim: Apico-basal polarity is essential for polarized membrane traffic.
source: Apico-basal polarity is also essential for polarized membrane traffic.
evidence: This is established knowledge in cell biology.

claim: Directed trafficking depends on the phosphoinositide composition of the plasma membrane, the cytocortex and various Rab proteins.
source: Directed trafficking depends on the phosphoinositide composition of the plasma membrane, the cytocortex and various Rab (Ras-related in brain) proteins.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature (Weisz and Rodriguez-Boulan, 2009; Eaton and Martin-Belmonte, 2014; Blasky et al., 2015; Rodriguez-Boulan et al., 2005; Croisé et al., 2014).

claim: Epithelial cell polarity and polarized membrane traffic require differential enrichment of PI(4,5)P2 and PI(3,4,5)P3 in the apical and basolateral membranes, respectively.
source: Epithelial cell polarity and polarized membrane traffic require differential enrichment of phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate (PI(4,5)P2) and phosphatidylinositol 3,4,5-trisphosphate (PI(3,4,5)P3) in the apical and basolateral membranes, respectively (Di Paolo and De Camilli, 2006; Martin-Belmonte and Mostov, 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: PI(4,5)P2 levels are controlled by Pten, which converts PI(3,4,5)P3 into PI(4,5)P2.
source: PI(4,5)P2 levels are controlled by Pten (Phosphatase and tensin homolog deleted on chromosome ten), which converts PI(3,4,5)P3 into PI(4,5)P2, by the type I phosphatidylinositol 4-phosphate 5-kinase Skittles (Sktl), which produces PI(4,5)P2 from phosphatidylinositol 4-phosphate (PI4P), and by Ocrl (Oculocerebrorenal syndrome of Lowe), which dephosphorylates PI(4,5)P2 into PI4P (de Renzis et al., 2002; Knirr et al., 1997; Maehama et al., 2004; Claret et al., 2014; Gervais et al., 2008; Worby and Dixon, 2014; Balakrishnan et al., 2015; Weixel et al., 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Skittles (Sktl) produces PI(4,5)P2 from phosphatidylinositol 4-phosphate (PI4P).
source: PI(4,5)P2 levels are controlled by Pten (Phosphatase and tensin homolog deleted on chromosome ten), which converts PI(3,4,5)P3 into PI(4,5)P2, by the type I phosphatidylinositol 4-phosphate 5-kinase Skittles (Sktl), which produces PI(4,5)P2 from phosphatidylinositol 4-phosphate (PI4P), and by Ocrl (Oculocerebrorenal syndrome of Lowe), which dephosphorylates PI(4,5)P2 into PI4P (de Renzis et al., 2002; Knirr et al., 1997; Maehama et al., 2004; Claret et al., 2014; Gervais et al., 2008; Worby and Dixon, 2014; Balakrishnan et al., 2015; Weixel et al., 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Ocrl dephosphorylates PI(4,5)P2 into PI4P.
source: PI(4,5)P2 levels are controlled by Pten (Phosphatase and tensin homolog deleted on chromosome ten), which converts PI(3,4,5)P3 into PI(4,5)P2, by the type I phosphatidylinositol 4-phosphate 5-kinase Skittles (Sktl), which produces PI(4,5)P2 from phosphatidylinositol 4-phosphate (PI4P), and by Ocrl (Oculocerebrorenal syndrome of Lowe), which dephosphorylates PI(4,5)P2 into PI4P (de Renzis et al., 2002; Knirr et al., 1997; Maehama et al., 2004; Claret et al., 2014; Gervais et al., 2008; Worby and Dixon, 2014; Balakrishnan et al., 2015; Weixel et al., 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Pten activity is antagonistic to that of the type IA phosphatidylinositol three kinase (Pi3K), which is enriched at basolateral membranes and converts PI(4,5)P2 into PI(3,4,5)P3.
source: Pten activity is antagonistic to that of the type IA phosphatidylinositol three kinase (Pi3K), which is enriched at basolateral membranes and converts PI(4,5)P2 into PI(3,4,5)P3 (Gassama-Diagne et al., 2006; Peng et al., 2015; Balakrishnan et al., 2015; Gao et al., 2000; Goberdhan et al., 1999; Huang et al., 1999).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: PI(4,5)P2 can bind to pleckstrin homology (PH)-domains of FERM proteins and β-Spectrins.
source: PI(4,5)P2 can bind to pleckstrin homology (PH)-domains of FERM proteins and β-Spectrins (Yoon et al., 1994; Harlan et al., 1995), thereby linking the plasma membrane to the cytocortex and to the trafficking machinery (Barroso-González et al., 2009; Ramel et al., 2013; Beck and Nelson, 1998; Holleran and Holzbaur, 1998; Kang et al., 2009).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: PI(4,5)P2 is directly implicated in the regulation of exocytosis.
source: Moreover, PI(4,5)P2 is directly implicated in the regulation of exocytosis (Milosevic et al., 2005; Gong et al., 2005; Massarwa et al., 2009; Rousso et al., 2013) and in all forms of endocytosis (Antonescu et al., 2011; Mayinger, 2012; Jost et al., 1998).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: PI(4,5)P2 is implicated in all forms of endocytosis.
source: Moreover, PI(4,5)P2 is directly implicated in the regulation of exocytosis (Milosevic et al., 2005; Gong et al., 2005; Massarwa et al., 2009; Rousso et al., 2013) and in all forms of endocytosis (Antonescu et al., 2011; Mayinger, 2012; Jost et al., 1998).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Loss of Crb in SGs disrupts the apical cytocortex.
source: We identified Crb as a novel regulator of apical secretion and maintenance of the apical microvilli in SG cells. We show that loss of Crb in SGs disrupts the apical cytocortex, apical secretion and the apical trafficking machinery, including the organization of Rab6-, Rab11- and Rab30-positive apical compartments, and the localization of their effector Myosin V (MyoV) (Lindsay et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by data showing reduced apical F-actin and βH-Spec upon Crb knockdown (Figure 2A-F).

claim: Loss of Crb in SGs disrupts apical secretion.
source: We identified Crb as a novel regulator of apical secretion and maintenance of the apical microvilli in SG cells. We show that loss of Crb in SGs disrupts the apical cytocortex, apical secretion and the apical trafficking machinery, including the organization of Rab6-, Rab11- and Rab30-positive apical compartments, and the localization of their effector Myosin V (MyoV) (Lindsay et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by data showing SerpCBD-GFP retention upon Crb knockdown (Figure 1K-M).

claim: Loss of Crb in SGs disrupts the organization of Rab6-, Rab11- and Rab30-positive apical compartments.
source: We identified Crb as a novel regulator of apical secretion and maintenance of the apical microvilli in SG cells. We show that loss of Crb in SGs disrupts the apical cytocortex, apical secretion and the apical trafficking machinery, including the organization of Rab6-, Rab11- and Rab30-positive apical compartments, and the localization of their effector Myosin V (MyoV) (Lindsay et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by data showing loss of apical Rab6-YFP, Rab11-YFP, and Rab30-YFP upon Crb knockdown (Figure 4A-F').

claim: Loss of Crb in SGs disrupts the localization of Myosin V (MyoV).
source: We identified Crb as a novel regulator of apical secretion and maintenance of the apical microvilli in SG cells. We show that loss of Crb in SGs disrupts the apical cytocortex, apical secretion and the apical trafficking machinery, including the organization of Rab6-, Rab11- and Rab30-positive apical compartments, and the localization of their effector Myosin V (MyoV) (Lindsay et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by data showing reduced apical MyoV upon Crb knockdown (Figure 3A,B,D).

claim: Loss of Crb impairs the function of the apical secretory machinery.
source: Loss of Crb increases apical levels of PI(4,5)P2, a phenotype that requires the activity of Pten, and impairs the function of the apical secretory machinery.
evidence: This statement is supported by data showing SerpCBD-GFP retention and loss of apical Rab proteins upon Crb knockdown.

claim: The defects in apical secretion upon loss of Crb are accompanied by the formation of a novel apical membrane compartment enriched in PI(4,5)P2 and phospho-Moe containing microvilli.
source: These defects are accompanied by the formation of a novel apical membrane compartment, which emerges as a solitary intracellular sac of PI(4,5)P2- and phospho-Moe-enriched apical membrane containing microvilli.
evidence: This statement is supported by confocal imaging showing phospho-Moe and PI(4,5)P2 accumulation in sacs (Figures 2H, 5C) and TEM showing intracellular vesicles with microvilli (Figure 2L').

claim: The PAMS are reminiscent to intracellular vacuolar structures found in patients with MVID (microvillus inclusion disease).
source: This compartment is reminiscent to intracellular vacuolar structures found in patients with MVID (microvillus inclusion disease), a fatal genetic disease characterized by lack of microvilli on the surface of enterocytes (www.omim.org/entry/251850).
evidence: This is a comparison based on morphological similarity and knowledge of MVID pathology.

claim: MVID is a fatal genetic disease characterized by lack of microvilli on the surface of enterocytes.
source: This compartment is reminiscent to intracellular vacuolar structures found in patients with MVID (microvillus inclusion disease), a fatal genetic disease characterized by lack of microvilli on the surface of enterocytes (www.omim.org/entry/251850).
evidence: This statement is supported by a reference to OMIM database.

claim: Crb acts as an apical hub to couple phospholipid metabolism and cytoskeleton scaffolds with apical membrane traffic.
source: We conclude that Crb acts as an apical hub to couple phospholipid metabolism and cytoskeleton scaffolds with apical membrane traffic.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data showing Crb's effects on PI(4,5)P2 levels, cytoskeleton organization, and Rab protein localization.

claim: The Crb complex is dispensable for maintenance of apico-basal polarity in larval salivary glands (SGs).
source: The Crb complex is dispensable for maintenance of apico-basal polarity in larval salivary glands (SGs)
evidence: This is a section heading supported by data showing that canonical polarity markers remain properly localized upon Crb knockdown (Figure 1D-G).

claim: KD of Crb effectively reduces apical levels of Crb, Sdt and DPatj in larval SGs.
source: Strikingly, although the KD of Crb effectively reduces apical levels of Crb, Sdt and DPatj (Figure 1B–C' and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C,D,Q), it does not affect the overall morphology of SGs, as determined by phalloidin staining (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This statement is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: KD of Crb does not affect the overall morphology of SGs, as determined by phalloidin staining.
source: Strikingly, although the KD of Crb effectively reduces apical levels of Crb, Sdt and DPatj (Figure 1B–C' and Figure 1—figure supplement 1C,D,Q), it does not affect the overall morphology of SGs, as determined by phalloidin staining (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This statement is supported by phalloidin staining data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: The SGs lacking Crb are shorter when compared to their control counterparts.
source: Yet, the SGs lacking Crb are shorter when compared to their control counterparts (Figure 1—figure supplement 1R, Figure 1—figure supplement 1—source data 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by quantification data shown in the referenced figure.

claim: Similar results to Crb KD were observed upon RNAi-mediated KD of Sdt.
source: Similar results were observed upon RNAi-mediated KD of Sdt (Figure 1—figure supplement 1R–X).
evidence: This statement is supported by data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: KD of Crb or Sdt does not alter the polarized distribution of Bazooka (Baz), aPKC, Par-6, Disc large (Dlg), Yurt (Yrt) and Coracle (Cora).
source: Interestingly, KD of Crb or Sdt does not alter the polarized distribution of any canonical apical or basolateral polarity marker tested, including Bazooka (Baz, Figure 1D,E), aPKC (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E,F), Par-6 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1G,H and Y,Z), Disc large (Dlg, Figure 1F,G and Figure 1—figure supplement 1AA, BB), Yurt (Yrt) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1I,J) and Coracle (Cora, Figure 1—figure supplement 1K,L).
evidence: This statement is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: The Crb protein complex is required for proper apical secretion in larval SGs.
source: The Crb protein complex is required for proper apical secretion in larval SGs
evidence: This is a section heading supported by data showing SerpCBD-GFP retention upon Crb or Sdt knockdown.

claim: The time necessary to reach the pupal stage is prolonged upon depletion of Crb.
source: In fact, when compared to control larvae, the time necessary to reach the pupal stage is prolonged upon depletion of Crb (Figure 1H, Figure 1—source data 1) or Sdt (Figure 1—figure supplement 1KK, Figure 1—figure supplement 1—source data 2).
evidence: This statement is supported by pupariation rate data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: Upon silencing of Crb or Sdt, Cad99C and CD8-RFP do not localize properly at the apical membrane but instead localize in intracellular vesicles.
source: We found that upon silencing of Crb or Sdt, Cad99C and CD8-RFP do not localize properly at the apical membrane but instead localize in intracellular vesicles (Figure 1I,J and Figure 1—figure supplement 1CC,DD,M,N and EE,FF).
evidence: This statement is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: Loss of Crb or Sdt results in intracellular retention of SerpCBD-GFP at the apical aspect.
source: Notably, while SerpCBD-GFP is barely detectable upon overexpression in control glands, loss of Crb or Sdt results in an obvious intracellular retention of SerpCBD-GFP at the apical aspect (Figure 1K–M, Figure 1—source data 2 and 3; and Figure 1—figure supplement 1 GG, HH, and LL, Figure 1—figure supplement 1—source data 3 and 4).
evidence: This statement is supported by live imaging data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: Glycoprotein secretion is impaired upon loss of Crb or Sdt, as revealed by intracellular retention of peanut-agglutinin-GFP (PNA-GFP).
source: In support of the idea that Crb is necessary for efficient apical secretion, we also found that glycoprotein secretion is impaired upon loss of Crb or Sdt, as revealed by intracellular retention of peanut-agglutinin-GFP (PNA-GFP, Figure 1—figure supplement 1O,P and II,JJ), which can bind to glycoproteins produced by the SGs (Korayem et al., 2004; Theopold et al., 2001; Tian and Ten Hagen, 2007).
evidence: This statement is supported by live imaging data shown in the referenced figures and citations about PNA-GFP function.

claim: KD of Crb does not affect the localization of the zonula adherens (ZA) in SG cells.
source: We did not find any abnormalities in the localization of the zonula adherens (ZA) of Crb-deficient SG cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 2A',C' arrowheads).
evidence: This statement is supported by TEM data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: pSJs are morphologically abnormal in SGs of Crb KD animals, showing many interruptions and disorganized regions.
source: In contrast to ZA, pSJs are morphologically abnormal in SGs of Crb KD animals, showing many interruptions (Figure 1—figure supplement 2C, green highlight) and disorganized regions (Figure 1—figure supplement 2D).
evidence: This statement is supported by TEM data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: Defects in pSJs were corroborated by reduced immunostaining of Sinuous (Sinu) and Kune-kune (Kune).
source: Defects in pSJs were corroborated by reduced immunostaining of some pSJ components, including Sinuous (Sinu, Figure 1—figure supplement 2E,F), Kune-kune (Kune, Figure 1—figure supplement 2G,H), while others, such as Fasciclin3 (Fas3, Figure 1—figure supplement 2I,J), Dlg (Figure 1F,G), Lachesin-GFP and Nervana2-GFP (not shown) were not affected.
evidence: This statement is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: KD of Crb does not increase dye penetration into the lumen in a Dextran-permeability assay.
source: Interestingly, KD of Crb does not increase dye penetration into the lumen when compared to control glands (Figure 1—figure supplement 2K–L'), suggesting that the epithelium is tight.
evidence: This statement is supported by Dextran-permeability assay data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: KD of Fas3-GFP enhances the diffusion of 10 kDa-Dextran into the gland lumen.
source: In contrast, KD of Fas3-GFP, used as a positive control, enhances the diffusion of 10 kDa-Dextran into the gland lumen (Figure 1—figure supplement 2M,M').
evidence: This statement is supported by Dextran-permeability assay data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: Crb regulates apical membrane organization via the apical cytocortex.
source: Crb regulates apical membrane organization via the apical cytocortex
evidence: This is a section heading supported by data showing effects of Crb KD on F-actin, βH-Spec, and Moe.

claim: KD of Crb decreases apical levels of F-actin in SG cells.
source: We found that KD of Crb decreases apical levels of F-actin (Figure 2A–C, Figure 2—source data 1) and βH-Spec (Figure 2D–F, Figure 2—source data 2).
evidence: This statement is supported by quantification data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: KD of Crb decreases apical levels of βH-Spec in SG cells.
source: We found that KD of Crb decreases apical levels of F-actin (Figure 2A–C, Figure 2—source data 1) and βH-Spec (Figure 2D–F, Figure 2—source data 2).
evidence: This statement is supported by quantification data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: KD of Crb-GFP-A induces accumulation of Moe and phospho-Moe into a single sac per cell localized right below the apical domain.
source: Moreover, KD of Crb-GFP-A induces accumulation of Moe, as well as its active form phospho-Moe, into a single sac per cell localized right below the apical domain (Figure 2G,H, arrows, Video 3 and not shown).
evidence: This statement is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in the referenced figures and video.

claim: The sacs formed upon Crb KD are positive for the apical transmembrane protein Stranded at second tagged with YFP (Sas-YFP).
source: These sacs are also positive for the apical transmembrane protein Stranded at second tagged with YFP (Firmino et al., 2013) (Sas-YFP, Figure 2I,J) suggesting that they have an apical plasma membrane identity.
evidence: This statement is supported by live imaging data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: KD of Crb has no evident effects on the organization of α-Tubulin or α-Spectrin.
source: On the other hand, KD of Crb has no evident effects on the organization of α-Tubulin or α-Spectrin (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G–J).
evidence: This statement is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: Cells from Crb-depleted SGs display intracellular vesicles containing microvilli.
source: Strikingly, cells from Crb-depleted SGs display intracellular vesicles containing microvilli (Figure 2L', arrowheads and Figure 2—figure supplement 2), which seem to correspond to the Sas-YFP positive sacs described above (Figure 2J).
evidence: This statement is supported by TEM data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: In Crb-deficient SGs, the density of apical microvilli is dramatically reduced.
source: Moreover, in Crb-deficient SGs, the density of apical microvilli is dramatically reduced (Figure 2K',L', brackets, and M, Figure 2—source data 3).
evidence: This statement is supported by TEM data and quantification shown in the referenced figures.

claim: The number of microvilli per micron adjacent to the apical plasma membrane is 8.0 ± 1.219 in control vs. 4.125 ± 1.446 in Crb-deficient cells.
source: The number of microvilli per micron adjacent to the apical plasma membrane is 8.0 ± 1.219 in control vs. 4.125 ± 1.446 in Crb-deficient cells (mean ± SD, p<0.0001, n = 8).
evidence: This statement is supported by quantification of TEM data.

claim: Microvilli are shorter in Crb-deficient cells.
source: This difference is even bigger when measured at 1 μm above the plasma membrane, 7.75 ± 1.222 in control vs. 2.850 ± 1.441 in Crb-deficient cells (mean ± SD, p<0.0001, n = 8), indicating that microvilli are also shorter in Crb-deficient cells.
evidence: This statement is inferred from the quantification data showing fewer microvilli at 1 μm above the membrane.

claim: Crb-deficient SG cells exhibit large intracellular vesicles that probably correspond to enlarged lysosomes.
source: In addition, Crb-deficient SG cells exhibit large intracellular vesicles not present in control SGs, which probably correspond to enlarged lysosomes (asterisks in Figure 2L' and in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B'C'; see also Figure 1—figure supplement 2C blue highlight).
evidence: This statement is supported by TEM data and is speculative about the identity of the vesicles.

claim: Live imaging of SGs incubated with Lysotracker showed that KD of Crb or Sdt increases lysosomal activity.
source: Indeed, live imaging of SGs incubated with Lysotracker showed that KD of Crb or Sdt increases lysosomal activity (Figure 2—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This statement is supported by Lysotracker staining data shown in the referenced figure.

claim: Loss of βH-Spec prompts formation of PAMS marked by phospho-Moe.
source: Indeed, loss of βH-Spec (Figure 2—figure supplement 4A,B) prompts formation of PAMS marked by phospho-Moe (Figure 2—figure supplement 4C,D).
evidence: This statement is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: In SGs deficient in βH-Spec, Crb remains apical and additionally localizes to the PAMS.
source: Moreover, in SGs deficient in βH-Spec, Crb remains apical and additionally localizes to the PAMS (Figure 2—figure supplement 4E,F).
evidence: This statement is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: Crb localizes to the apical domain independently of βH-Spec.
source: These results indicate that Crb localizes to the apical domain independently of βH-Spec while βH-Spec requires Crb to be organized at the apical cytocortex.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that Crb remains apical in βH-Spec KD cells.

claim: βH-Spec requires Crb to be organized at the apical cytocortex.
source: These results indicate that Crb localizes to the apical domain independently of βH-Spec while βH-Spec requires Crb to be organized at the apical cytocortex.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that βH-Spec is lost from the apical domain in Crb KD cells.

claim: Crb regulates apical membrane organization via MyosinV.
source: Crb regulates the apical membrane organization via MyosinV
evidence: This is a section heading supported by data showing effects of Crb KD on MyoV localization and secretion.

claim: The PAMS are reminiscent to microvilli-containing vesicles found in samples from MVID patients, which is linked to mutations in the MYO5b gene.
source: The PAMS described above are reminiscent to microvilli-containing vesicles found in samples from MVID (microvillus inclusion disease) patients, which is linked to mutations in the MYO5b gene (Müller et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a comparison based on morphological similarity and knowledge of MVID pathology, supported by a citation.

claim: Similar inclusions to PAMS are found in animal models of MVID.
source: Similar inclusions are found in animal models of MVID (Sidhaye et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: MyosinV (MyoV) is a processive motor that transports cargos along F-actin.
source: MyosinV (MyoV) is a processive motor that transports cargos along F-actin (Reck-Peterson et al., 2000) and is a component of the apical secretory machinery in epithelia (Massarwa et al., 2009; Reck-Peterson et al., 2000; Li et al., 2007; Pocha et al., 2011a).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: MyoV is a component of the apical secretory machinery in epithelia.
source: MyosinV (MyoV) is a processive motor that transports cargos along F-actin (Reck-Peterson et al., 2000) and is a component of the apical secretory machinery in epithelia (Massarwa et al., 2009; Reck-Peterson et al., 2000; Li et al., 2007; Pocha et al., 2011a).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: In photoreceptor cells, Crb regulates apical transport of Rhodopsin-1 by interacting with MyoV.
source: Moreover, in photoreceptor cells, Crb regulates apical transport of Rhodopsin-1 by interacting with MyoV (encoded by the gene didum) (Pocha et al., 2011a).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous literature.

claim: The KD of Crb decreases apical MyoV in SG cells.
source: Indeed, the KD of Crb decreases apical MyoV (Figure 3A,B,D, Figure 3—source data 1 and 2).
evidence: This statement is supported by quantification data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: Overexpression of MyoV-GFP in Crb-deficient glands does not rescue its apical localization.
source: Importantly, overexpression of MyoV-GFP in Crb-deficient glands does not rescue its apical localization (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1—source data 1 and 2).
evidence: This statement is supported by quantification data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: KD of βH-Spec decreases apical MyoV.
source: Furthermore, KD of βH-Spec also decreases apical MyoV (Figure 3A,C,D, Figure 3—source data 1 and 3) as well as apical secretion as revealed by the apical retention of SerpCBD-GFP (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–C, Figure 3—figure supplement 2—source data 1 and 2).
evidence: This statement is supported by quantification data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: KD of βH-Spec impairs apical secretion as revealed by the apical retention of SerpCBD-GFP.
source: Furthermore, KD of βH-Spec also decreases apical MyoV (Figure 3A,C,D, Figure 3—source data 1 and 3) as well as apical secretion as revealed by the apical retention of SerpCBD-GFP (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–C, Figure 3—figure supplement 2—source data 1 and 2).
evidence: This statement is supported by quantification data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: βH-Spec acts downstream of Crb to maintain apical MyoV.
source: This suggests that βH-Spec acts downstream of Crb to maintain apical MyoV.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that both Crb and βH-Spec KD decrease apical MyoV.

claim: MyoV KD impairs secretion of SerpCBD-GFP, which accumulates at the apical aspect of MyoV-deficient SG cells.
source: Indeed, we found that MyoV KD impairs secretion of SerpCBD-GFP, which in turn accumulates at the apical aspect of MyoV-deficient SG cells (Figure 3K–M, Figure 3—source data 4 and 5).
evidence: This statement is supported by quantification data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: Formation of PAMS can be a consequence of defects in the apical secretory machinery.
source: These results suggest that formation of PAMS can be a consequence of defects in the apical secretory machinery.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that MyoV KD induces PAMS formation.

claim: Crb is a novel regulator of the apical Rab machinery in larval SGs.
source: Crb is a novel regulator of the apical Rab machinery in larval SGs
evidence: This is a section heading supported by data showing effects of Crb KD on Rab protein localization.

claim: The Rab protein family is a major regulator of intracellular membrane traffic routes.
source: The Rab protein family is a major regulator of intracellular membrane traffic routes (Wandinger-Ness and Zerial, 2014; Pfeffer, 2013) and MyoV is known to interact with Rab6 and Rab11 (Lindsay et al., 2013; Li et al., 2007; Iwanami et al., 2016), which play an important role in apical membrane trafficking and recycling (Khanal et al., 2016; Iwanami et al., 2016; Chung and Andrew, 2014; Li et al., 2007; Satoh et al., 2005; Pelissier et al., 2003).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: MyoV is known to interact with Rab6 and Rab11.
source: The Rab protein family is a major regulator of intracellular membrane traffic routes (Wandinger-Ness and Zerial, 2014; Pfeffer, 2013) and MyoV is known to interact with Rab6 and Rab11 (Lindsay et al., 2013; Li et al., 2007; Iwanami et al., 2016), which play an important role in apical membrane trafficking and recycling (Khanal et al., 2016; Iwanami et al., 2016; Chung and Andrew, 2014; Li et al., 2007; Satoh et al., 2005; Pelissier et al., 2003).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Rab6 and Rab11 play an important role in apical membrane trafficking and recycling.
source: The Rab protein family is a major regulator of intracellular membrane traffic routes (Wandinger-Ness and Zerial, 2014; Pfeffer, 2013) and MyoV is known to interact with Rab6 and Rab11 (Lindsay et al., 2013; Li et al., 2007; Iwanami et al., 2016), which play an important role in apical membrane trafficking and recycling (Khanal et al., 2016; Iwanami et al., 2016; Chung and Andrew, 2014; Li et al., 2007; Satoh et al., 2005; Pelissier et al., 2003).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Loss of Crb affects the localization of Rab6-YFP, Rab11-YFP and Rab30-YFP.
source: Strikingly, we found that loss of Crb affects the localization of a subset of Rab proteins, namely Rab6-YFP, Rab11-YFP and Rab30-YFP.
evidence: This statement is supported by live imaging data shown in Figure 4A-F'.

claim: The apically localized pools of Rab6-YFP, Rab11-YFP and Rab30-YFP are reduced upon Crb KD.
source: Specifically, the apically localized pools of these Rab proteins are reduced (Figure 4A–F', and Videos 4–6), while the basal pools are not affected significantly.
evidence: This statement is supported by live imaging data shown in the referenced figures and videos.

claim: Crb KD does not alter the organization of Rab1-YFP.
source: The effects on this subset of Rab proteins are specific, as Crb KD does not alter the organization of other Rab proteins, like Rab1-YFP (Figure 4G–H', Video 7, and Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by live imaging data shown in the referenced figures and video.

claim: Total protein levels of Rab6-YFP, Rab11-YFP and Rab30-YFP do not change significantly upon Crb KD.
source: Importantly, total protein levels of these Rab proteins do not change significantly upon Crb KD (Figure 4I).
evidence: This statement is supported by Western blot data shown in the referenced figure.

claim: KD of βH-Spec removes the apical pools of Rab6-YFP and Rab11-YFP.
source: Strikingly, KD of βH-Spec only removes the apical pools of Rab6-YFP and Rab11-YFP (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A–D), while the apical Rab30-YFP and the intracellular Rab1-YFP compartments are not affected (Figure 4—figure supplement 2E–H).
evidence: This statement is supported by live imaging data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: The apical localization of Rab6 and Rab11 require a functional apical cytocortex.
source: Thus, the apical localization of Rab6 and Rab11 require a functional apical cytocortex.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that βH-Spec KD removes apical Rab6 and Rab11.

claim: KD of Rab11-YFP results in formation of PAMS in larval SG cells.
source: More importantly, loss of Rab11 results in formation of PAMS in larval SG cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 3D'', arrows).
evidence: This statement is supported by live imaging data shown in the referenced figure.

claim: Defects in the apical secretory machinery can induce the formation of PAMS.
source: Hence, defects in the apical secretory machinery can induce the formation of PAMS.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that Rab11 KD induces PAMS formation.

claim: βH-Spec acts downstream of Crb to organize the apical localization of Rab6-YFP and Rab11-YFP.
source: Moreover, βH-Spec acts downstream of Crb to organize the apical localization of Rab6-YFP and Rab11-YFP.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that both Crb and βH-Spec KD remove apical Rab6 and Rab11.

claim: Crb regulates apical membrane levels of PI(4,5)P2.
source: Crb regulates apical membrane levels of PI(4,5)P2
evidence: This is a section heading supported by data showing increased PI(4,5)P2 upon Crb KD.

claim: Phospho-Moe can bind to PI(4,5)P2 via its PH-domain.
source: Phospho-Moe can bind to PI(4,5)P2 via its PH-domain (Yonemura et al., 2002; Fiévet et al., 2007; Fehon et al., 2010; Roch et al., 2010) and the phosphoinositide composition of a membrane regulates Rab protein activity, as well as the localization of cytoskeleton proteins (Wandinger-Ness and Zerial, 2014; Tan et al., 2015; Mayinger, 2012; Liem, 2016; Bennett and Healy, 2009; Fehon et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The phosphoinositide composition of a membrane regulates Rab protein activity and the localization of cytoskeleton proteins.
source: Phospho-Moe can bind to PI(4,5)P2 via its PH-domain (Yonemura et al., 2002; Fiévet et al., 2007; Fehon et al., 2010; Roch et al., 2010) and the phosphoinositide composition of a membrane regulates Rab protein activity, as well as the localization of cytoskeleton proteins (Wandinger-Ness and Zerial, 2014; Tan et al., 2015; Mayinger, 2012; Liem, 2016; Bennett and Healy, 2009; Fehon et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: PI(4,5)P2 is enriched in the apical membrane of larval SGs.
source: Live imaging of larval SGs shows that PI(4,5)P2 is enriched in the apical membrane (Figure 5B,H, Figure 5—source data 1), as previously observed in late 3rd instar SGs (Rousso et al., 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by live imaging data shown in the referenced figures and a citation to previous literature.

claim: Quantification of PLCδ-PH-EGFP fluorescence intensity of Crb-deficient SGs shows an increase in apical levels of PI(4,5)P2.
source: Importantly, quantification of PLCδ-PH-EGFP fluorescence intensity of Crb-deficient SGs shows an increase in apical levels of PI(4,5)P2 (Figure 5C,H, Figure 5—source data 2).
evidence: This statement is supported by quantification data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: PI(4,5)P2 localizes in the PAMS.
source: Additionally, PI(4,5)P2 localizes in the PAMS (Figure 5C), which are also positive for phospho-Moe (Video 8).
evidence: This statement is supported by live imaging data shown in the referenced figure and video.

claim: Expression of ptenRNAi in Crb KD glands effectively suppresses both the accumulation of PI(4,5)P2 and PAMS formation.
source: Expression of ptenRNAi (Ramachandran et al., 2009) in Crb KD glands effectively suppresses both the accumulation of PI(4,5)P2 as measured by PLC-PH-EGFP fluorescence, and PAMS formation (Figure 5D,E,H, Figure 5—source data 3 and 4), while expression of pi3K92ERNAi enhances the accumulation of PI(4,5)P2 and PAMS formation (Figure 5F,G,H, Figure 5—source data 5 and 6).
evidence: This statement is supported by quantification data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: Expression of pi3K92ERNAi enhances the accumulation of PI(4,5)P2 and PAMS formation.
source: Expression of ptenRNAi (Ramachandran et al., 2009) in Crb KD glands effectively suppresses both the accumulation of PI(4,5)P2 as measured by PLC-PH-EGFP fluorescence, and PAMS formation (Figure 5D,E,H, Figure 5—source data 3 and 4), while expression of pi3K92ERNAi enhances the accumulation of PI(4,5)P2 and PAMS formation (Figure 5F,G,H, Figure 5—source data 5 and 6).
evidence: This statement is supported by quantification data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: KD of Sktl is less effective in suppressing PAMS upon Crb KD than knocking-down Pten.
source: Interestingly, KD of Sktl, another enzyme producing PI(4,5)P2, is less effective in suppressing PAMS upon Crb KD than knocking-down Pten (Figure 5—figure supplement 1I–M, Figure 5—figure supplement 1—source data 3–6).
evidence: This statement is supported by quantification data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: Over-expression of Pten2 induces accumulation of PI(4,5)P2 and formation of PAMS.
source: To corroborate the importance for Pten to mediate the phenotype induced by loss of Crb, we found that over-expression of Pten2 induces accumulation of PI(4,5)P2 and formation of PAMS (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A,B), while over-expression of Sktl results in strong defects in SG morphology (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A,C).
evidence: This statement is supported by live imaging data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: Ex vivo incubation of SGs with VO-OHpic, a chemical inhibitor of Pten activity, eliminates the PAMS from Crb-deficient cells.
source: Moreover, ex vivo incubation of SGs with VO-OHpic, a chemical inhibitor of Pten activity (Mak et al., 2010), eliminates the PAMS from Crb-deficient cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1N–R, Figure 5—figure supplement 1—source data 7–10).
evidence: This statement is supported by live imaging data shown in the referenced figures and a citation about the inhibitor.

claim: Pten is the main source of PI(4,5)P2 involved in the formation of the PAMS upon Crb depletion.
source: Thus, our findings suggest that Pten is the main source of PI(4,5)P2 involved in the formation of the PAMS upon Crb depletion.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the genetic interaction data showing that Pten KD suppresses PAMS formation.

claim: Quantification of the fluorescence intensity revealed no significant change in the PI(3,4,5)P3 apical-to-lateral ratio in Crb KD glands.
source: The signal of this probe at the plasma membrane is very weak and quantification of the fluorescence intensity revealed no significant change in the PI(3,4,5)P3 apical-to-lateral ratio in Crb KD glands (Figure 5—figure supplement 2D–F, Figure 5—figure supplement 2—source data 1).
evidence: This statement is supported by quantification data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: Quantification of the Pten2-GFP fluorescence intensity revealed a decrease in the apical-to-lateral ratio in Crb and Sdt KD glands.
source: Interestingly, quantification of the Pten2-GFP fluorescence intensity revealed a decrease in the apical-to-lateral ratio in Crb and Sdt KD glands (Figure 5K and data not shown, Figure 5—source data 7), suggesting that Crb is required to ensure Pten levels at the apical membrane (Figure 5I,J, arrowheads).
evidence: This statement is supported by quantification data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: Crb is required to ensure Pten levels at the apical membrane.
source: Interestingly, quantification of the Pten2-GFP fluorescence intensity revealed a decrease in the apical-to-lateral ratio in Crb and Sdt KD glands (Figure 5K and data not shown, Figure 5—source data 7), suggesting that Crb is required to ensure Pten levels at the apical membrane (Figure 5I,J, arrowheads).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that Pten2-GFP apical-to-lateral ratio decreases upon Crb KD.

claim: KD of Crb severely decreases the apical localization of Ocrl.
source: Moreover, KD of Crb severely decreases the apical localization of Ocrl (Figure 5M,N, Figure 5—source data 8 and 9).
evidence: This statement is supported by quantification data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: KD of Ocrl modestly increases the apical levels of PI(4,5)P2.
source: KD of Ocrl modestly increases the apical levels of PI(4,5)P2 (Figure 5O–Q, Figure 5—source data 10 and 11), yet this is not accompanied by formation of PAMS.
evidence: This statement is supported by quantification data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: Apical accumulation of PI(4,5)P2 and formation of PAMS induced by the loss of Crb result from a combined effect of increased Pten activity and loss of Ocrl from the apical membrane.
source: Together, these results show that apical accumulation of PI(4,5)P2 and formation of PAMS induced by the loss of Crb, seem to result from a combined effect of increased Pten activity and loss of Ocrl from the apical membrane upon loss of Crb.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the genetic interaction data showing effects of Pten and Ocrl on PI(4,5)P2 levels.

claim: Efficient apical secretion requires the control of PI(4,5)P2 metabolism by Crb.
source: Efficient apical secretion requires the control of PI(4,5)P2 metabolism by Crb
evidence: This is a section heading supported by data showing that Pten KD rescues secretion defects in Crb KD glands.

claim: Apical secretion of SerpCBD-GFP in Crb-deficient SGs is restored upon concomitant KD of Pten.
source: Live imaging analysis revealed that apical secretion of SerpCBD-GFP in Crb-deficient SGs is restored upon concomitant KD of Pten (Figure 6A–D,G, Figure 6—source data 1 to 4), while KD of Pi3K92E alone, or in combination with Crb KD, induces a stronger apical retention of SerpCBD-GFP than the one observed in Crb-deficient SGs (Figure 6B,E–G, Figure 6—source data 5 and 6).
evidence: This statement is supported by quantification data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: KD of Pi3K92E alone, or in combination with Crb KD, induces a stronger apical retention of SerpCBD-GFP than the one observed in Crb-deficient SGs.
source: Live imaging analysis revealed that apical secretion of SerpCBD-GFP in Crb-deficient SGs is restored upon concomitant KD of Pten (Figure 6A–D,G, Figure 6—source data 1 to 4), while KD of Pi3K92E alone, or in combination with Crb KD, induces a stronger apical retention of SerpCBD-GFP than the one observed in Crb-deficient SGs (Figure 6B,E–G, Figure 6—source data 5 and 6).
evidence: This statement is supported by quantification data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: KD of Pten efficiently suppresses the loss of the apical pools of Rab11-YFP and Rab30-YFP observed upon Crb depletion.
source: Similarly, KD of Pten efficiently suppresses the loss of the apical pools of Rab11-YFP (Figure 6H–K,N, Figure 6—source data 7 to 10) and Rab30-YFP (Figure 6O–R,U, Figure 6—source data 13 to 16) observed upon Crb depletion.
evidence: This statement is supported by quantification data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: KD of Pi3K92E in control cells induces loss of apical Rab11-YFP.
source: Interestingly, KD of Pi3K92E in control cells induces loss of apical Rab11-YFP (Figure 6L,N, Figure 6—source data 11 and 12), but has no effect on Rab30-YFP localization (Figure 6S,U, Figure 6—source data 17 and 18).
evidence: This statement is supported by quantification data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: Over-expression of Pten2 in the SGs induces the loss of apical pools of Rab11-YFP and Rab30-YFP.
source: Additionally, over-expression of Pten2 in the SGs induces the loss of apical pools of Rab11-YFP and Rab30-YFP (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A–D).
evidence: This statement is supported by live imaging data shown in the referenced figures.

claim: Crb function is required to organize the apical cortex and to control the phosphoinositide metabolism, which in turn regulates the apical Rab protein machinery (Rab11-YFP, Rab30-YFP and possibly Rab6-YFP).
source: Thus, Crb function is required to organize the apical cortex and to control the phosphoinositide metabolism, which in turn regulates the apical Rab protein machinery (Rab11-YFP, Rab30-YFP and possibly Rab6-YFP).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the genetic interaction data showing that Pten KD rescues Rab protein localization defects in Crb KD glands.

claim: KD of Crb in the SGs slightly reduces the amount of food intake, yet this reduction is not statistically significant.
source: We found that KD of Crb in the SGs, as well as KD of Pi3K92E, slightly reduces the amount of food intake (Figure 6V, Figure 6—source data 19), yet this reduction is not statistically significant (one-way ANOVA followed by Tukey's multiple comparisons test).
evidence: This statement is supported by quantification data shown in the referenced figure and statistical analysis.

claim: Concomitant KD of Crb and Pten significantly increases the larval food intake when compared to controls.
source: Interestingly, concomitant KD of Crb and Pten significantly increases the larval food intake when compared to controls (Figure 6V).
evidence: This statement is supported by quantification data shown in the referenced figure.

claim: Animals with SG-specific depletion of Crb take longer to pupariate than control animals.
source: Hence, while animals with SG-specific depletion of Crb take longer to pupariate than control animals (Figure 6W), those with additional Pten KD pupariate faster than those with Crb KD alone.
evidence: This statement is supported by pupariation rate data shown in the referenced figure.

claim: Animals with additional Pten KD pupariate faster than those with Crb KD alone.
source: Hence, while animals with SG-specific depletion of Crb take longer to pupariate than control animals (Figure 6W), those with additional Pten KD pupariate faster than those with Crb KD alone.
evidence: This statement is supported by pupariation rate data shown in the referenced figure.

claim: The pupariation of Pi3K92E KD animals is similar to the one of Crb-deficient animals.
source: Moreover, the pupariation of Pi3K92E KD animals is similar to the one of Crb-deficient animals, while concomitant KD of Crb and Pi3K92E delays the pupariation even more.
evidence: This statement is supported by pupariation rate data shown in Figure 6W.

claim: Concomitant KD of Crb and Pi3K92E delays the pupariation even more than Crb KD alone.
source: Moreover, the pupariation of Pi3K92E KD animals is similar to the one of Crb-deficient animals, while concomitant KD of Crb and Pi3K92E delays the pupariation even more.
evidence: This statement is supported by pupariation rate data shown in Figure 6W.

claim: Crb is essential for apical membrane homeostasis, apical secretion and physiological function of larval SGs.
source: Taken together, our results demonstrate that Crb is essential for apical membrane homeostasis, apical secretion and physiological function of larval SGs.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data showing effects of Crb KD on PI(4,5)P2 levels, secretion, and pupariation.
